withdraw.missing: a formula form of sig.warning_lamp that reads the lamp's facing: sig_warning_lamp [track, colour, mode, facing] (facing ∈ {front, rear, side}, as the atom's contract already lists). The condition u4, with the words it borrows from u5 (DEF-NRS-484A-480-3: 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'), holds only when the approaching vehicle is making use of a flashing red warning lamp facing front. Core's evaluator reads sig_warning_lamp only as [track, colour] or [track, colour, mode], so 'visible from the front' cannot be written. Writing a lit red flashing lamp of any facing is a weaker fact on a condition span. It would trigger the duty for a vehicle showing only rear- or side-facing red flashers as it closes from behind, a vehicle the law does not cover. So the missing form decides whether the duty to stop arises at all, and toward which approaching road users it is owed. Red and flashing are carried; only the facing lacks a form.
nearest: sig.warning_lamp: contract 'a warning lamp lit; colour ∈ {red, blue, amber, white}, mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}, facing ∈ {front, rear, side}', but its formula forms take [track, colour] or [track, colour, mode] only (Core/Language/Semantics.lean:181-182), so the facing is in the world (WarningLamp.facing) and no formula reads it
rel.visible: 'Not a stand-in for: ... a lamp being lit — a visible vehicle may show no lamp and a lit lamp may be hidden', so it cannot carry which way the lamp faces
rel.bearing: places the subject ahead of the approaching vehicle (already read for u1), not the direction a lamp faces
